text:
We checked “4 err 2 warn transformations” and found 4 issues in the InDesign file that are likely causing the problems in Frontify, plus 4 that may change how it looks. Here’s what to change:

Likely causing the problems

1. Image is flipped or skewed
Frontify can’t reproduce flipped or skewed images, so they’ll look different or break when edited.
Where: images “230209_FRO2301_NYC_15.jpg” (page 2) and “Frontify_Linkedin-Cover-Employee_1584x396.png” (page 2)
• Double-click to select the image inside the frame, then choose Object > Transform > Clear Transformations (or set the shear angle to 0° and remove the flip).
• If you need the flipped look, save a flipped copy of the image file instead.
Learn more

2. Text frame has no paragraph style
Frontify uses paragraph styles to format text and decide what can be edited.
Where: text frames “Image in frame rotationand frame…” (page 1), “in frame flip verticalimage only…” (page 2)
• Select the frame and apply a paragraph style in Window > Styles > Paragraph Styles (any style except [Basic Paragraph] or [No Paragraph Style]).
Learn more

3. Image frame is flipped or skewed
Frontify can’t reproduce flipped or skewed frames, so the image will look different or break when edited.
Where: the image “230209_FRO2301_NYC_15.jpg” (page 2)
• Select the image frame and choose Object > Transform > Clear Transformations (or set the shear angle to 0° and remove the flip).
Learn more

4. Linked image missing from the package
The document links to an image that isn’t in the package, so Frontify can’t show it.
Where: the image “logo_FÃ¶rderturm_original.png” (page 1)
• Relink any missing images in Window > Links.
• Package again with File > Package with "Copy Linked Graphics" checked.
Learn more

May change how it looks

5. Image frame is rotated
Rotation works, but the frame may look slightly different in Frontify than in InDesign.
Where: the image “Frontify_guidelines_grey.png” (page 1, rotated 19°)
• Check the result in Frontify. If it looks off, remove the rotation from the frame.
Learn more

6. Image is rotated
Rotation works, but the image may look slightly different in Frontify than in InDesign.
Where: the image “Frontify_guidelines_grey.png” (page 1, rotated -24°)
• Check the result in Frontify. If it looks off, save a rotated copy of the image and place it unrotated.
Learn more

7. Paragraph Composer used
The Adobe Paragraph Composer breaks lines differently from browsers, so text may reflow in Frontify.
Where: the paragraph style “[Basic Paragraph]”, used on page 1
• In the paragraph style, go to Justification and set Composer to Adobe Single-line Composer.
Learn more

8. Unused images in the package
These files aren’t used in the document and only make the package bigger.
Where: the image “logo_Förderturm_original.png”
• Delete the unused files from the Links folder before zipping the package.
Learn more

Once that’s done, package the document again with File > Package, zip the package folder and upload it to Frontify.
